title: Sticker Size Guide: PNG, 300 DPI, Die-Cut & Cricut Upload
description: Sticker file sizes for print and cut: 300 DPI PNGs, common 2–3 in prints, die-cut vs kiss-cut, white borders, pixel math, and Cricut Design Space upload steps.
summary: Export a square PNG with a transparent background outside your art. For sharp home or shop printing, size the file in pixels as inches × DPI (for example 3×3 in at 300 DPI = 900×900 px). PiCraft also gives a 2048×2048 px transparent PNG and a ready 3×3 in print file with a white die-cut border.

sections.heading: Sticker file specs at a glance
paragraphs: Sticker art is usually a PNG with a clear edge for cutting. Sharp print depends on enough pixels for the inches you print.

after: These match the [Sticker Maker](/create/sticker-maker) outputs. Scale the print file down in your software for smaller stickers, or use the 2048 px file when you need extra room to edit.

sections.heading: Pixels, inches and DPI
paragraphs: Pixel width or height = inches × DPI. At 300 DPI, 3 in equals 900 px per side. Enlarging a small file lowers effective DPI and softens edges.
300 DPI is a common target for small stickers with text or thin lines. Redbubble lists minimum pixels per sticker tier and recommends 2800×2800 px so all four sticker sizes stay enabled.

table.caption: Example square sticker sizes at 300 DPI (pixels = inches × 300)
rows: Common shop size; PiCraft print download

after: The Sticker Maker FAQ notes that 2–3 inch stickers are the most common for home and small-shop use. Generate at the size you plan to print, or start from the 3×3 in file and scale down—not up—for smaller results.

sections.heading: Die-cut vs kiss-cut and the white border
paragraphs: Die-cut stickers are cut through the backing sheet to the shape of the art, often with a narrow white margin around the illustration so the blade has a clean path. Kiss-cut stickers are cut through the sticker layer only, leaving them on a larger backing sheet (common for sticker sheets and roll labels).

PiCraft draws a continuous white die-cut border and removes the area outside it, so the PNG is transparent beyond that edge. That matches how many home Print Then Cut workflows expect the cut line to sit just outside the visible art.

Commercial sticker sheets may use different margin rules; check your printer's template if you are not cutting at home. The [kiss-cut vs die-cut stickers](/blog/kiss-cut-vs-die-cut-stickers) guide compares what seven printers ask for in the file.

sections.heading: Cricut Design Space and Print Then Cut limits
paragraphs: For Cricut Print Then Cut, upload a PNG (or JPG) via Upload → Upload Image. On desktop, choose Flat Graphic when you want a full-color Print Then Cut image with a home printer. PiCraft files already have the background removed, so you can upload and save without re-tracing unless you need to tweak the cut path.

Print Then Cut reserves space on the page for sensor marks, so the maximum cuttable area is smaller than the paper. On US Letter (8.5×11 in), Cricut documents a maximum cuttable area of about 9.94×7.44 in on Explore and Maker series machines—your sticker layout must fit inside that window along with registration marks.

If Design Space warns that the image is too large, resize on the Canvas or change the page under Settings → Print Then Cut Settings. Finish print and cut in one session so registration marks stay aligned.
after: See [sticker artwork for print and cut](/blog/sticker-artwork-print-and-cut) for a full checklist, and [Stickers and merch](/categories/stickers-and-merch) for related formats.

sections.heading: Common sizing mistakes
items: Printing below 300 DPI equivalent: a 400×400 px file stretched to 3 in prints soft and jagged.
Scaling in the print dialog: leaving "fit to page" on changes the real size; use 100% scale for the 900×900 px file when you want exactly 3 in.
Missing transparency: JPG backgrounds become white rectangles on cut files; use PNG.
Ignoring Print Then Cut maximums: a sticker larger than the letter-size cut area needs a smaller design or a larger page size.

sections.heading: Make sticker art at the right size
paragraphs: The [Sticker Maker](/create/sticker-maker) exports a 900×900 px (3×3 in at 300 DPI) transparent PNG plus a 2048×2048 px version, both with a white die-cut border and no background cleanup on your side. Optional text is limited to 30 characters; proofread before you print.

Each generation is one design. Lay out several PNGs on one sheet in Cricut Design Space or your print software for a mixed sticker sheet. To check that a PNG you already have is transparent and at the right size, use the free [image size checker](/tools/image-size-checker).

faq.q: What size should a sticker PNG be for printing?
faq.a: Match pixels to the printed inches at 300 DPI: multiply inches by 300 for each side. A 3×3 in sticker is 900×900 px. PiCraft includes that size plus a 2048×2048 px file for larger prints or editing.

faq.q: What is the difference between die-cut and kiss-cut stickers?
faq.a: Die-cut cuts each sticker to its shape through the backing. Kiss-cut cuts the sticker layer only and leaves shapes on a shared backing sheet, typical for sticker sheets. PiCraft art is aimed at die-cut and Print Then Cut with a white outline.

faq.q: Can I use PiCraft stickers with Cricut Print Then Cut?
faq.a: Yes. Upload the PNG, choose Flat Graphic for a full-color Print Then Cut image, print on sticker paper and cut around the white border. Confirm the design fits the Print Then Cut area for your paper size before you make the project.

faq.q: How big can one Print Then Cut sticker be on letter paper?
faq.a: On 8.5×11 in letter stock, Cricut lists a maximum cuttable area of about 9.94×7.44 in for Explore and Maker series, including space for sensor marks. A square sticker cannot use the full 11 in height.

faq.q: Does PiCraft add cut lines to the file?
faq.a: No. The transparent edge outside the white border is the cut path. Regenerate if pale grey at the edge disappears when the background is removed.
